newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia not to impose 15 pct tax on local Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia not to impose 15 pct tax on local Eurobonds.

text.p: The Russian government will not subject regional Eurobond issues to the 15 percent tax recently levied on government securities, First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin said on Friday.
"There is no difference of opinion on the 15 percent tax -- it should be lifted," Potanin told journalists. "The question is how to do it technically and legally."
He said the Finance Ministry was now working on the problem.
He said the government had decided to drop an earlier proposal to charge an 0.8 percent fee for registering regional Eurobond.
Potanin said regional borrowing through Eurobonds must not exceed 30 percent of a region's annual revenues and servicing Eurobond debt must not exceed 15 percent of revenues.
"I think it is a wise regulation, it will discipline the regions," he said.
Several Russian cities and regions, including Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod, are preparing Eurobond issues, but the plans had been delayed because Russian tax law was unclear.
Potanin did not say when a government document regulating regional Eurobond issues would be signed.
